evidence.pattern: SJ01 pressure level associated with later DL RSSI/SNR degradation
evidence.reason: Discovery association did not preserve magnitude or sign in characterization.

option_A.interpretation: The pressure–RF association should remain screened out because it did not reproduce with stable direction and magnitude across development periods.
alternative_explanations: The original association may be a development-period fluctuation that does not generalize across time.
The pressure variable may be acting as a proxy for a broader time-varying environmental regime rather than as the relevant physical driver.
The apparent relation may depend on how RF degradation is defined, even if the original exploratory association looked coherent.
falsification_tests: require a newly registered formulation to preserve effect direction across prespecified contiguous temporal blocks.
test whether the qualitative association persists under prespecified alternative RF outcome definitions.
only a newly frozen formulation may be tested on future data; the failed formulation remains screened out.

option_B.interpretation: The exploratory association is not stable across development periods and should not be promoted.
alternative_explanations: The initial association may be a development-period fluctuation.
The relationship may depend on an unmodeled time-varying regime.
falsification_tests: Require sign and effect-direction stability across prespecified contiguous temporal blocks.
Retain the candidate as screened out unless a newly registered formulation is tested without reusing failed evidence as confirmation.

evidence.pattern: CU01 humidity level inversely associated with DL MCS
evidence.reason: Association was not stable after trend and diurnal-cycle screening.

option_A.interpretation: The humidity–DL MCS association should remain screened out because it was not robust to temporal-cycle control.
alternative_explanations: A shared time-of-day structure may create the inverse association.
A slow temporal trend may make humidity and DL MCS appear related even when their short-term variations are not linked.
The discrete RF outcome may respond to other time-varying conditions that happen to co-occur with humidity changes.
falsification_tests: compare candidate events with controls matched to the same clock-time structure.
test the residual association after a prespecified temporal-trend and diurnal adjustment.
require the adjusted direction to remain stable across contiguous temporal blocks.

option_B.interpretation: The apparent association is not robust to temporal trend or diurnal-cycle control and should not be promoted.
alternative_explanations: Shared time-of-day structure may explain both atmospheric and RF variation.
Slow temporal drift may create an association without a direct atmospheric-to-RF relationship.
falsification_tests: Use same-clock or seasonally matched controls.
Test residual association after prespecified temporal-trend adjustment.

evidence.pattern: Cold-humid-calm atmospheric regime associated with degraded RF state
evidence.reason: 30-minute block-level risk reversed between discovery and characterization.

option_A.interpretation: The candidate lacks stable event-level temporal independence and should not be promoted.
alternative_explanations: Serial dependence may inflate block-level support.
Repeated observations from the same regime may create pseudoreplication.
falsification_tests: Re-express support using refractory event episodes rather than row counts.
Require directionally consistent results across contiguous temporal folds.

option_B.interpretation: The cold–humid–calm regime should remain screened out because block-level association did not survive an event-level temporal-independence requirement.
alternative_explanations: Serial dependence may inflate apparent support within long-lived regimes.
The regime label may pool heterogeneous episodes whose RF behavior differs across time.
Block-level enrichment may arise from repeated sampling of the same episode rather than reproducible event-level coupling.
falsification_tests: rebuild support from independent regime episodes separated by a prespecified refractory interval.
require event-level direction to remain stable across contiguous temporal folds.
compare independent regime episodes with temporally matched non-event controls.

evidence.pattern: Multivariate atmospheric transition followed by sharp RF-quality drop
evidence.reason: Block-level enrichment was robust across many thresholds, but RF drops were not more frequent after atmospheric transitions than before them.

option_A.interpretation: The candidate fails temporal precedence and should not be promoted as a precursor.
alternative_explanations: The atmospheric and RF events may reflect a shared regime.
The atmospheric transition may be coincident with or downstream of RF change.
falsification_tests: Compare prespecified pre-event and post-event RF entry counts around independent atmospheric events.
Require post-event excess to preserve direction across temporal folds.

option_B.interpretation: The multivariate transition should remain screened out because robust enrichment without preserved temporal precedence is insufficient for a precursor claim.
alternative_explanations: RF degradation may occur before, during, or after the atmospheric transition with no stable ordering.
Temporal clustering may create enrichment around transitions without directional dependence.
A broad event window may capture coincident processes that cannot be causally ordered from the current evidence.
falsification_tests: compare independent pre-event and post-event RF entries using a frozen event window.
repeat the directionality test using only temporally independent atmospheric transition episodes.
test whether the same atmospheric signature remains associated after the RF event, which would favor a shared-context interpretation.

evidence.pattern: Lower 60-minute SJ01 humidity variability before RF-quality drops relative to same-clock controls
evidence.reason: The signal preserved sign but failed FDR replication, post-event negative control, and characterization control-support requirements.

option_A.interpretation: The matched trajectory association fails the registered robustness controls and should not be promoted.
alternative_explanations: The association may reflect persistent context rather than a directional precursor.
The result may be sensitive to outcome definition or control support.
falsification_tests: Apply prespecified same-clock matched controls and multiplicity correction.
Use post-event trajectories as a negative-control check for temporal precedence.

option_B.interpretation: The lower-humidity-variability pattern should remain screened out because the matched trajectory evidence did not satisfy the registered robustness and negative-control requirements.
alternative_explanations: The same context may persist before and after RF events, which would weaken temporal precedence.
The association may depend on the RF outcome definition used to identify degradation events.
Matched controls may have insufficient support in some temporal regions, making the apparent trajectory difference unstable.
falsification_tests: require the candidate to weaken or disappear after the RF event if it is to be interpreted as a precursor.
repeat the prespecified analysis across alternative RF event definitions.
evaluate the full registered feature family under the same multiple-testing correction rather than selecting the favorable trajectory alone.

evidence.pattern: Rapid warming and drying transition at SJ01 followed by apparent RF degradation enrichment
evidence.reason: Block-level enrichment did not preserve temporal ordering: discovery had more RF entries before than after the atmospheric transition.

option_A.interpretation: The warming-and-drying transition should remain screened out because apparent enrichment did not preserve pre/post temporal ordering.
alternative_explanations: Temporal clustering may create enrichment even when the RF event is not downstream of the atmospheric transition.
The transition may be coincident with, rather than antecedent to, the RF degradation process.
A broader environmental regime may generate both transition signatures and RF events without a direct directional link.
falsification_tests: require post-event RF entries to exceed pre-event entries under the frozen event definition.
repeat the test using only temporally independent transition episodes.
require the direction of the pre/post contrast to remain stable across contiguous development blocks.

option_B.interpretation: The apparent enrichment does not preserve pre/post temporal ordering and should not be promoted.
alternative_explanations: A shared environmental regime may create enrichment without directional precedence.
Temporal clustering may produce apparent block-level association.
falsification_tests: Require post-only RF entries to exceed pre-only entries under the registered event window.
Do not access the confirmatory holdout for a candidate that already fails development directionality.
